And after reading it, I still have to wonder what I read and did I like it. I would really like to hear what your thoughts are. Have any of you read this? What did you think? Concrete Underground Leave your comments on [...]. This book will be towards the bottom of my Books in the Pile.

I just finished reading this book, all told over a period of 2 days much to the detriment of both my job and personal life, but I would not give that time back for anything. It was intriguing, and made me ravenous for more. I can honestly say that while reading this, my whole being was absorbed into the story line a first for any book I have ever read. Moxie Mezcal is an absolute genius of the literary arts and I surmise will be one of the greatest writers of our time. I plan on recommending this book to ever person I know that despite the distractions of everyday life still enjoys great writing.

Just finished reading Mezcal's Concrete Underground, and hope this is not the last novel we see from this creative talent. I love D's do what thou will attitude, and the suspense still hanging in the aethers at the end of the story. Very subtle clues haunt the sequence of events. Depictive modules are used in an unusual manner. Nothing is as it seems.

Avoiding predictable twists, the story line is pushed to incalculable boundaries.

Guerrilla Fiction as described in the author's manifesto seems a promising nouveau genre which I HOPE to see more of in the near future!

LVX! 93!
summary: Punk mystery with passion, sex and violence at its best

reviewText:
At the recommendation of Marc Horne (whose new book I am about to jump into), I read Concrete Underground by Moxie Mezcal. It's a fast-paced gritty novel, with a very violent bent. I've been enjoying indie fiction lately, and this did not disappoint.  The books is definitely interesting and well written. Think Palahniuk meets film noir with a new-age punk-emo vibe.

As it turns out, I eventually got thrown off the ride that Marc describes as a "... noir plot [that] loops it into a feedback cycle until it breaks." Still struggling with the end though (not sure what ended up happening, if anything at all). I don't hold that against the author though.

Lots of fun and very layered. Give it a shot.

`Concrete Underground' knocked me out. It takes the noir plot and loops it into a feedback cycle until it breaks. It embraces the implausibility of the hero and squeezes horror out of it. Fast, sexy fun is laid on top of a growing layer of scar tissue on human faces until you can't tell the difference anymore. It wears its influences on its sleeve and even walks you through them, but it makes something new out of them.  A true 21st century novel.
This book was very weird. I searched for murder mystery and this came up. Not the kind of book I normally read.
I flew through this book. It is fast paced with so many twists and turns. Kept me guessing until the very end. Very intelligently written with cool dialogue and interesting characters.

I believe this was my first foray into guerrilla fiction and I can't say I'm all that impressed. I missed a lot of the allusions and I'm still not sure what was real and how much exactly I didn't catch. I certainly don't have answers for any of the questions at the end of the book. I guess reading should be mentally challenging but I don't think I was ready for this. However, it is entertaining, in a sadistic kind of way.
This book kept me riveted the whole time.  I couldn't wait to see  what happened next.  Mystery suspense very unusual story that keeps you captivated.  Recommended if you like a good mystery.

This is not a good book in fact it is not a book in the classical sense instead it reads like a stream of consciousness flowing with connected and disconnected free associations from the mind of a hallucinating post-surgical patient battling a morphine high. In this story the patient never wakes up. I can't recommend this for casual readers or for anyone younger than twenty-one. Pretty rough stuff. I will not read it again.
One of the strangest and weird books I have ever read. I thougt it would get better , but it never happened .

Kept me interested but nothing major ever really happens and just when you think your getting to the good part you getcomplete mind blowing crazy ending that's hard to follow and just completely ruins the book

This is the most unconventional book that I have ever read. Not completely sure how much I like it, although I could hardly stop reading it.

What's in that room???
This was a strange book with a lot of weirdness... Eh, however I wasn't angry that I had invested my time in reading it.

I finished this book over the weekend finally.  Maybe it's the way I read it in bits and pieces when I had time, but I'm still not exactly sure what happened in it - what was real and what wasn't.  It was over-the-top plotting with some of the strangest characters I've encountered recently.

That said, I liked it.  Quite a bit, actually.  I thought it was written well and formatted decently (there were a few errors but nothing that pulled me out of the story), and I wanted to get back to it when I wasn't reading it; I thought about the story during and after reading it.  I wanted to know what would happen next and I never fully expected anything that happened.  Like I said, I'm still not sure about exactly what really happened, but I certainly don't regret reading it.  Far from it, I might read it again and see if I can figure it out in a second go-through...

Definitely was a great reading! The plot was good as well...one bad thing was certain (grammatical errors) were present throughout the book. D went through so much and Max had a real crazy wild lifestyle

very interesting story with allot of twist and turns, at times it can be difficult to read as I feel that the editing job could use some work.  It may just be me but I kinda hate the main character and enjoyed read about him getting hurt, but the interactions between him and the other characters is more then enough to keep me reading. The ending felt clumsy but all in all it was a good read if you like roller coasters this is a good book for you.

This book was one of the most bizarrely strangest I've ever read. It reminds me of a Clockwork Orange.  It was good and I would read it again.  It had lots of twist and turns with unexpected surprises!!!  Too many characters that were hard to keep straight.  Overall, Mezcal is a likable pshyco and a great author whom I look forward to reading more of his work!!!

This story was intriguing at times, but was not the easiest story to follow.  The characters were all unlikable, so it was hard to get drawn in and care about how the story ended up.  I found myself forcing myself to finish the book just to be done with it.  It seems like it was written with an intent to constantly shock and throw twists into it, without any focus on keeping a consistent storyline.  All that said, the book did have its moments and the premise was interesting.

What drew me to this book was the (possibly intentional) play on words of the title. All I could see was the Velvet Undergound of my youth. It's a sure treat when I can find a story using counter culture as a plot premiss.

You meet D at the start. As he shares his thoughts on those around him, you are shown the angst he holds deeply inside. He is a heavy drinker and drinks so much, you almost wonder how he is still able to function.

The twists are plentiful. The ideas are thought provoking. I would almost call it the 1984 of the 21st century. Almost because although mentioned, the author doesn't explore this avenue of thought to it's fullest. It's more like a treatise on the effect of the digital age on humanity and social interactions as a whole.

If you have read Shutter Island and liked it, trust me, you will like this one too.
summary: Bizarre in the Best Possible Way

reviewText: Great mystery, fun read, great characters.  I was slightly confused at the end, but a good mystery should make one think.

This book was free and it was still over-priced.  It was simply a waste of time to read it, but I kept thinking he was going to actually complete a thought somewhere and was curious as to when/where.  He didn't.  Disjointed, hodge-podge plot that doesn't even have an ending.  It was probably an attempt to be clever, but it was far from it.  If there was a zero rating, I'd give it that.

This was a hard book to read.  You have to concentrate to follow the characters and action and to wrap your mind around what is happening in this fantasy.  Often times you wonder whose dream you're following and whether it really is a dream.  This was not my favorite read in quite a while and I'm not sure if I'd try another by this author.

The ONLY reason I finished this book is because I try to finish every book I start.  I  was so lost I couldn't figure out what was going on. Then when i thought the book was over it started up again. Oh well glad it's over. On to something else.

I love reading a book that isn't just the standard cookie cutter plot skeleton fleshed out with varying character names and typical situations. I love when an author isn't afraid to take a story to the extremes. Moxie Mezcal is definitely one of my new favorite authors. This book isn't going to be for everyone, but I fully enjoyed it and I would say at least try it before writing it off for being different!

After having finishing reading this, about all I can say is that it was way too strange for me. I still can't tell you what happened. Too many twists and turns, and I don't know what was real and what was the main character's imagination.

I'm glad it was free.

While I get the pulp fiction end of the other reviewers, I couldn't even finish this book.  I made it thorugh 25% of the book and was so completely bored that I couldn't even motivate myself to pick it back up.  There are sooooo many characters in the first part of the story, and the author fails to get involved with each of them before moving on to the next.  I can see how the story has some potential, but after the first quarter of the book, the story has still gone nowhere and I refuse to continue to read to figure out where it's going.  Further, it seems as though the author had several great "thoughts" about what should be in the book, but failed to organize those thoughts.  It almost seems like a very rought draft of several different potential story ideas.  Very scatter brained and boring!

This was the first book I downloaded for Kindle, and I got it because it was free. What a deal! The writing is smart and compelling. It's no more vulgar than you would expect a bit of pulp fiction to be. It's got a great "whodunnit" quality, but the author also pushes back against genre, as one of the above reviews notes. I'm deeply taken with Moxie Mezcal. I recommend others to check out Moxie's website, where you can hear the soundtracks listed in the book. Oh, and this is a perfect book for a digital format. At the end of the book the author offers a handful of questions to help the reader solve the puzzle, and the search feature on the Kindle opens up so many more connections than I would have been able to piece together normally.

An excellent novel.

While I have to give the author kudos for writing this, sadly the only good thing I can say about it is it was different. Unlike anything I have ever read before. There was far too much going on, too many redundancies and twists that in my opinion were thrown in just for the sake of having a twist.
The writing itself was all right. Lots of typos and errors. Maybe I just don't understand "Guerrilla Fiction" as the author describes this sort of work. Guerrilla Fiction doesn't need to justify itself.
Granted the pulp-fiction style was there, but anything else this could have been described as just lurked in the shadows.
Read it for yourself, you may like it. Sadly, I didn't.

Honestly, I don't know why I like this book.  The protagonist, D, gets beat up more than a shirt in an old fashioned washing machine.  But he is so snarky that I wanted to slap him around a little myself.  And yet, and yet, I just kept pressing "next page" because I wanted to know what was going on.  The author offers extra pages to help us figure out the plot somewhat by the Socratic method, and that's when the book is over!  It's kind of scifi and kind of a mystery and kind of a quixotic quest for some kind of justice and kind of a conspiratory thriller.  And it's FREE!  I think you will either like it or hate it, but  you will only lose some time.

I downloaded this book for free so at least I can't complain about the price. Too much violence for me. I couldn't follow the plot at all, too much going on in this book. The ending was more more violence and confusion.

I found this book to be full of horrid language and crude and offensive sexual acts.  Read it on my kindle because it was free.  Sorry I downloaded this one.  Confusing story line at times.  Hard to keep all the characters and their relationships to each other straight.  The main character keeps making huge leaps of intuition that are invariably correct, and it is difficult to follow how he could have figured that out.

Great read, perfect twists. Made my jaw drop numerous times. Witting writing, great attitudes and descriptions. I loved the way this book was written, definitely different from what I am use to and it is what caught my eye from the beginning and kept me giggling here and there at some points of description. I was never a big "mystery" fan but this book was GREAT. I definitely look forward to more from this author.
I thought this was another great free story.  The more I read the more I wanted to keep reading.

This story had me intrigued from the very beginning. Every character is unique and well defined, and the plot is unlike anything else I have read. The story flowed like a Hitchcock movie and had me guessing up until the very end. The protagonist, "D" is a far-from-perfect reporter who is well aware of his shortcomings. It was refreshing to read a story where the protagonist is not omnipotent or a superhero. I will be reading more from Moxie Mezcal.

Near the end of the book a character states her opinion of mysteries. "They always try to trick you, deliberately throwing extraneous plot lines just to confuse and misguide you, withholding important information until the last chapter, using vague and misleading descriptions so you don't notice something that should be plain as day." I can only assume that Mezcal was trying to be funny because this was the blueprint for his entire book. Confusing at points, melodramatic, and never enough information to make a good guess at what's going on. The ending is, well, literally unforeseeable.

So that was the critique but, everything else aside, I couldn't put this book down. The writing ticked me off at points and I wanted to slap most of the characters, however the plot was really enthralling. I turned every page because I really wanted to see what was on the next one and isn't that what we look for in a good book?

I'm more of a sci-fi/fantasy/horror fan, but when it's free, I'll try anything... And I am so glad I did. Plenty of others have given the synopsis, so I'll just stick to the review.

5 stars for writing style: Mr. (Ms?) Mezcal has a "punk-as-f***" in your face kind of style, and there are a few genuine moments of laugh-out-loud humor as well. Refreshing and fun to read, the story just flowed along easily.

3 stars for content: there are a few places of "what just happened?" or "Eww, I don't need to have that stuck in my head for the next three days" moments. The latter is forgivable from a rating perspective, but the former is not. It kills the pace for me when I have to re-read something or refer back to an earlier occurence.

Overall: 4 stars - can't beat the price either!
Not like anything I've read in a long time. Twists and turns, and then more twists and turns. Just plain fun.
I can't get through the first few chapters as the language is so offensive. Please let me know if anyone else found this to be true. I am not a prima dona but this language was just too much!

Is sat down ready for a great read and was disappointed.  I kept reading waiting for the story to get better but, alas this did not happen.  The book jumped around like a. Two year old.  The end was just that The end. I think with some maturity this author could grow

I got this one free for Kindle awhile back.  It's not a genre I usually read. I found this book interesting but frustrating at the same time. True to the genre (I guess?) all kind of weird stuff happened all the time--particularly murders and beatings of the poor narrator.  His abuse reminded me of the Timex watch commercials from long ago "he takes a licking but keeps on ticking".  I still don't know what was real and what wasn't because I guess D didn't either.  It was confusing and I definitely did not solve the mystery.  I loved having the music to go with each chapter, kind of like wine pairings at a nice dinner.  Overall, it was ok.  Probably not the genre for me and glad to have gotten it for free.

This book has some very original and fascinating characters. Parts of the plot were good and could really pull you into the story. But the plot is too jerky for me to enjoy the book as a whole. The ending was just disappointing. It read like something a college kid who was trying to be too clever would write.

While this is not a book that I would read again, I think the author has great potential and will look for another of her books in the future.
summary: Good parts but not great as a whole

reviewText: Concrete Underground is a mystery novel that is very different from mainstream mystery writers. You don't get all the answers at the end;in fact, after the last chapter the author gives you a list of clues to help you solve the mystery. That said, I throughly enjoyed this book, and will definitely read his future novels. The characters are unique and interesting, and Mezcal manages to maintain a cohesive, realistic feel to a story that has lots of twists and turns, with some scenes bordering on the bizarre. This book, as well as Mezcal's short stories, are available for free from other sources, including the author's website.

Concrete Underground had my interest peeked from beginning to end. The twists and turns of events kept my mind reeling in hopes of figuring out the plot. Far from disappointing, Moxie Mezcal delivers a hardcore mindgame.
I enjoyed this book.  It was different and I enjoy reading new authors.  I love the free books from Kindle. Sometimes if I enjoy them enough I'm hooked and will keep buying!

I happen to meet the author while near Old Faithful this fall.  He mentioned he had written a book set in Yellowstone and I said I would look for it.  Well, I couldn't put it down.  John Mecom is scientist turned mystery writer and readers of "The Caldera Incident" will be very glad he did.  The characters are well-drawn and interesting not cliched; the plot is thick and textured;and, the references about the park, its environs, habitat, and inhabitants are very informative and make one want to know more about Yellowstone.  I read this book in two days and can't wait for another one.

THE CALDERA INCIDENT is a well-constructed story, filled with lots of interesting biological and geological facts and written in an easy to read manner that keeps the reader engaged from the very first chapter to the last.  As a reader, I was eager to find out not just "who dunnit" but why.  How were the law officers and rangers going to solve the mystery, and what impact would the geography and geology of this interesting region have on the characters?  Dr. Mecom has satisfied me with this tale, weaving all factors together very well for a first-time author.  I eagerly look forward to reading more of his work.  P. Hansen

This book has it all--adventure, mystery, murder, revenge, good, evil, and romance. It is set in Yellowstone National Park and contains enough twists to keep you turning the pages. In fact, it was so good I read the entire book in a single evening. The only criticism is the name of the evil one (Gerald) but that's just me.
Fast-moving murder mystery set in an area that is clearly well-known to the author.  This book would make a great film!

This is the authors third book and I have read them all. John just keeps getting better and better with each story.  When jerry steinbach told me john had a new book out I put my current read on hold and was not disappointed..  Well done John. When is the next book going to be ready?  The story is engaging and the characters well developed.  I recommend this book to anyone who enjoys reading a good book

THE CALDERA INCIDENT is a fast moving, intricate murder mystery that is hard to put down. The multiple characters are believable and the plot plausible, especially in this era of political polarization.

  The backdrop of Yellowstone National Park is grounded in scientific fact. If one wants to know more about super-volcanos (probably the largest on the planet) and see photos and webcams on mudpots and steam vents, go to 'nps.gov/yell'.
summary: Boil and Bubble, Toil and Trouble

reviewText: John Mecom has written a spellbinding thriller in The Caldera Incident. He's a born story teller. Also,I enjoyed reading his descriptive narrative of a part of the U.S. about which I know very little.
summary: A new author finds his voice in Yellowstone

reviewText: Outstanding read from an author who has vast knowledge of the Yellowstone National Park enviorns and the technical/forensic background to create a super story.  His wildlife and animal expertise is evident.  A great murder mystery that will not let put down the book till finished.  Looking for John Mecom to follow this with another thriller.

I think this book is a great read...an exciting murder mystery that kept me constantly turning the pages until I finished! It is filled with super descriptions of wildlife and wilderness.  You can tell the author has a love for both. The book also held interesting (and understandable) forensic and technical information which was deftly woven into this well-told story.

This is a book for everyone.  I'm anxious to see what author, John Mecom will give us in the future.
The book is a very interesting mystery about a murder in Yellowstone National Park. The book provides very detailed descriptions of characters and scenery.

All I can say is "Wow."  I'll be thinking about this book (that I couldn't put down until I finished) for a long time.  People, this is definitely something you should read.  All I can say is that until around the 95% mark I didn't see that ending coming.  And at that point I just plain didn't know what to expect.

Funny?  Yes.  Comedy, no.  It's suspenseful and riveting.

Good book! Very funny and definately kept me reading to find out what happened in the end. I was very surprised by the ending, I didn't have it anywhere near figured out! Great first novel, I will be waiting for more from this author.

Bought this after a friend recommended it and after seeing the glowing reviews here.

I wasn't enamored.  It kind of struck me as a bad knock-off of A Catcher in the Rye.

To me, the ending was predictable.

With every book I pick up I hope for that "can't put it down" feeling, and that is exactly what I got from Four Years From Home. After I finished the book, I wanted to read it again to pick up on the clues that the author had planted throughout each chapter. Kudos to Enright for his debut novel and hopes for many more to follow.

I recall watching the movie "The Sixth Sense" and the "Aha!" moment at the end. I wanted to watch the movie again to see how the plot unfolded, how all the pieces fit together. Larry Enright leads the reader down a mysterious path, wondering, guessing and then tightly wraps up the plot in a neat package -  leaving one questioning why one was unable to figure it all out sooner.  You'll enjoy the story that begins as a light-hearted nostalgic recollection of sibling rivalry and ends with can't- put- the- book -down suspense.

TREMENDOUS! I ordered this book on a friend's recommendation.  My mom got to the book first and couldn't put it down.  Before I could pick it up, my daughter snagged it, then passed it on to a school friend.  Finally it came back home and I got to read it.  Character development (or should I say, deterioration...) was very well done, really draws the reader in.  It's sort of a surprise ending even if you pick up on the vague clues early on.  I have to agree with my daughter who says, "This would make a fantastic movie!"

My mom, daughter and I each have different genre preferences.  We all enjoyed this book.  A good read for everyone.

It would be too simple to call the Ryans a dysfunctional family when every family member is perfectly functional except Tom Ryan. This energetic, splenetic, and funny main character manages to be outrageous and purposeful at the same time. There is underlying mystery and suspense here, so taut that the humor is more than just an entertainment, it is relief. I had to plow through the last eighty pages because I could not wait to encounter the noblest member of the surprisingly functional Ryan Family. Four Years from Home

Upon getting into the meat of the story, I spent my time until the end of the book trying to guess the next event and, of course, the ending.  I only do that with books that hold my interest.  This is a good book that moves well and is full of thought provoking events and side stories.  A very enjoyable read.
Enjoyed this book because it moved quickly and the ending was a real surprise.  I thought I had it figured out but not quite.  The ending leaves you with "I'll be darned."

I loved this book. It takes you into the life of Tom who really has some issues with his brother but loves him whole heartedly. It was so interesting and family oriented that you just want the book to keep going, to find out what the rest of Tom's life was after this. I really enjoyed it and would recommend it to friends and family. A special thanks to the author. Keep up the great work and I will continue to read your books. I got this book for free on Amazon one day special but after reading it I would of gladly paid for it and it's sequel.
summary: Heart warming, funny, exciting, relatable, and definitely a page turner.

reviewText: I can't believe I actually finished this awful book...something kept me reading, maybe it was the hope it would get better.
Fast and easy transaction. Item arrived on time and product was just as advertised. I am very satisfied with product.

Rarely do I read a book a second time, but this one I did.  Great ending, but one with just enough ambiguity to keep you wondering.  Characters stayed with me long after the book was done.  Highly recommended.
I had a hard time following the plot.  I didn't care for ending, It left me hanging.  Is there another book coming out to finish the story.

First of all, this book isn't humorous.  There weren't any funny parts where I "laughed out loud."  If "Encyclopedia Brown" existed I would pay him a quarter to figure out how this book got published without an editor.

The main character Tom Ryan is the first born and a bully.  He sees himself as king of his family - and those are his redeeming qualities.  His youngest brother Harry is a boy so pure of heart that his parents and grandmother want him to become a Catholic Priest.  So of course Tom hates him and is always trying to get him in trouble.

Tom also has a Nazi fetish and is consumed (throughout the entire book) with imaginary fights against the Germans.  This gets really old really fast.  Maybe it fits somehow with the time period of the book.  The Vietnam War is in the background of the story.

Anywho, Harry dies unexpectedly, and Tom is sent to investigate what happened.  Harry went away to college almost 4 years earlier and has not contacted anyone in the family the entire time.  (Why no one drove the 2 hours to see what Harry's problem was is never explained.  I also find it highly improbable.)  Lo & behold, when Tom arrives at the college everyone thinks that he is Harry.  What is going on?

Is Harry dead?  Why does everyone think Tom is Harry?  I will be honest.  By this point in the book I no longer cared.  The best way to read this book is to follow the advice of several other reviewers: read the first & last chapter.  Don't worry.  The story will still make sense and you will save lots of time spent on skimming over imaginary battle scenes.
summary: How did this book end up in the "humor" category?

reviewText: This book sucked me in from the very beginning.  My theory on what was going on changed several times during the reading.  I definitely recommend this book and I will be looking for other books by this author.

Four Years From Home is the first book I've read by Larry Enright.

I was taken in from the very beginning by the character of Tom.  I liked his sarcasm and biting wit, but I also liked to hate him when he lied and cheated and manipulated to get what he wanted.  I believe that Enright did a good job with character development and that is why Tom is so unlikeable at times. Harry, on the other hand, Tom's youngest sibling, was a very likeable character from the beginning.  He seemed to have a good sense of self.  He let the things Tom did just roll off his back.  When Harry went off to college and wasn't heard from for four years that seemed quite out of character for him.  I knew something had to be going on besides studying at college, but the ending certainly surprised me.

When you read this story, be ready for a bumpy ride...sibling rivalry, jealousy, biting sarcasm, humor, pain, and the ultimate show of brotherly love!
summary: Be Ready for a Bumpy Ride!

reviewText: This book draws you in almost immediately and there were places where I thought I knew how it would end, and then I had another idea of how it would end, but I certainly never saw the real ending coming!  It drags slightly in a few places, but mostly keeps you interested, a real page turner and I had trouble putting it down.  I would recommend this to anyone who likes books with a mystery, and I guarantee you won't guess the ending.  Loved it!
summary: Wow, I did not see this coming!  Five stars!

reviewText: I found this book under my suggested buys after purchasing Francesca of Lost Nation , another great family saga. And I was delighted to buy Four Years From Home. Anyone who has a Catholic background will relate to this story especially those of us who tried to live right but somehow were always having to go to confession. This story also reminds us of how easy its is to judge others when we should be cleaning out our own "closets." I like this story because it is also about family. I give it five stars.

This story pulls you in through its exploration of a family, its interactions and memories and makes you think about your own memories.

What's real and what isn't.

Once you think you have this story figured out, guess again. Dive in, enjoy the ride!
summary: Dive in and enjoy the ride.

reviewText:
This has to be the strangest book I have ever read. Difficult to follow at times, yet I couldn't stop reading it.
The big problem with this book is THE ENDING, or the lack of it. I waanted to know more and I am so disappointed
about the finish.

Too bad the people who rated this book so low didn't read it all the way through or even finish it.  Yes, it does take some time to get through it and yes it does take full concentration to understand the story but if you give it a chance it turns out to be pretty good with a complicated story.  Complicated for the characters not the reader.  It is fasinating to read to conclusion.  I don't want to give anything away but I thought I had the end figured out but I was wrong.  You must give it a fair read and read it all the way though!  I am an avid reader and I don't like boring, stuffy or words that must be looked up in a dictionary and I liked this book so that means..it wasn't any of those things.

I found this to be an exceptional read.  Partly due to the fact that I grew up in the Pittsburgh area during the time the Ryan's, of the story, were growing up. My brother and I were die hard fans of the television series Combat, which was a driving theme in this book.  It also brought back all the angst during the Vietnam war and the draft (where numbers were picked at random and if you had an unlucky number and were not a college student you had to fight).

I wasn't sure how this would turn out until the very, very end of the book and I will probably reread to make sure that I catch all the nuances that I probably missed the first time around.

Job well done and and excellent book.  It will stay with me for a long, long time.

I guess that the best way to describe this book is that it is "a scattered mess", just like the main character.  Tom is very unlikable, and as the book progresses, you like him even less.  He is just crazy nuts, which of course is confirmed by the end of the book.

Like most other reviewers, I was tempted to put this book down and move on to another, as it was just a bunch of scattered ramblings that got more and more boring, and seemingly incoherent and useless as the book went on.  But yet there was just enough story line to keep my interest.

I figured that the tragic ending was going to be something like what it was.  I was convinced that there was no Harry to begin with, that Tom had just been living a double personality his whole life.  While it was not that simple, it was close.

It is too bad that with this book you can read the first 3 chapters, and then jump ahead to the last two chapters, and get more of a meaning of the book than if you were to read the whole thing.

Glad I finished it, but the plot really needs to be better connected.

Wow, one of the best books I think I've ever read. At first I enjoyed it purely for the humor and pace of the writing, but then the plot began to thicken... And now that I've finished, my head is still spinning from the punch I didn't see coming! Awesome read. Enright's writing implants you right into the story's setting, its humor effortlessly guiding you along an intriguing path to... well, that's the kicker. And it was a great kick! This one will be given out to family on Christmas for sure! Can't wait to read his next one. Bravo, Larry! Bravo.
summary: funny, exciting, and mysterious... with a twist

reviewText: Probably the best written Indie book I've read. Kept me engaged throughout, though sometimes I got a bit disoriented separating reality from fantasy - but as it turns out that was the point. So the plot did a great job of reflecting the main character. Not your average genre fiction.

Until after the first half of the book, I was in awe about how it was so memoir-like though I know it's fiction.  The naughty and witty first person accounts were fun to read up to a certain level.  It got corny and just too much at one point but I couldn't stop reading as it left me clueless as to what would happen. I'd say it was all worth it in the end.

I bought this because it was partnered with my book. Because mine is a memoir, I assumed Larry's book was also. So, imagine my surprise when,near the end, I finally figure out it wasn't ...just a great mystery with an interesting twist. Good, tight writing and I read it in one sitting...couldn't put it down. Good job!
Page-turning mystery with well-defined characters and a couple of twists.  Older readers will recongnise the dialog of family dynamics in the past.  Wish he would write more books.

Some of the reviews I read about this book said it was funny.  I didn't find that to be true.

The only reason I finished the book is because I kept hoping that it would get better.  It didn't.  I am so glad it wasn't very expensive.

Hats-off to author Larry Enright, his novel's characters capture the psychosocial formula, perfectly. The recipe results in a fabulously twisted plot. The author maintains the characters intricate personalities throughout his novel. A skill few authors master so well. Tom, the main character, is a complex jerk, this dynamic defines the mystery. The unpredictable rogue sends the reader into a tailspin of emotions, and then, just when you think you have it all figured out, the author smacks into another turn. Personally, I would classify, Four Years From Home within the mystery genre. However, the style, created emotions often, delegated to thrillers. The depth of the story came to me as an unexpected surprise. Prior comments I read had me convinced Four Years From Home was a humorous cultural book about an Irish immigrant family, oh, but, it was much more. Tom's first person account barred nothing. Instead, it fuelled my fascination, blatantly baring his socially unacceptable narcissism, and distorted ego driven views. His codependent family added to the layers of believability. I am a lover of the human element within any story, Four Years From Home, fed my love masterfully. Nevertheless, the mystery, and drama are not forgotten. I highly recommend this book to anyone whom enjoys a great multilayered read. Four Years from Home

Many "mysteries" follow a formula, and you can start to predict where they're going l-o-n-g before the curtain falls. Here's the opposite--a book that keeps you guessing from beginning to end. At first, it's a memoir of life in a raucous Irish Catholic family (fascinating to a girl who grew up in a Methodist household with one sister). Then tragedy strikes, and nothing is as it seems to be. I can't say much more without risk of spoilage, aside from the fact that I read the whole book in one sitting. Hats off to Mr. Enright for weaving such an intricate and intriguing tale.
I thoroughly enjoyed this book.  I was looking for something different and it definitely is different.  Not only could I not put the book down but I could not sit still.  Well worth the read.

Like other reviews have said, the author started out with a great idea but couldn't figure out how to execute it.  After a few chapters, I skimmed through a lot of the book.  I was a bit concerned that I wouldn't understand the ending after skimming so much, but to my surprise it had no effect.  You could read the first few chapters and the last few and have complete understanding of the story.  It's like the middle is all useless filler.  After awhile, it gets kind of boring reading about Tom's selfish, mean-spirited pranks and Harry's pious goodness; they all blend together.  The ending was interesting but was very disjointed from the rest of the book.  I think the author was trying to pull a classic, "Wow, never saw THAT coming!" shocker, but it just didn't flow well.  Just poorly executed.  For .99 it killed some time, but it's nothing I would really recommend.

I'm a suspense guy.  Thrillers and mysteries and the less frequent sci-fi/fantasy escape.  So, when I sat down with Larry Enright's dramatic narrative "Four Years From Home", I did so with admitted reluctance.  But a good friend had recommended it to me, and I didn't have another book queued up, so . . .

Nine brisk-paced and nothing-else-accomplished hours later I turned the last page and smiled, as intensely satisfied as I've been with a book in years. What a fantastic accomplishment. What an incredible read.

Here's what blew me away: the anti-hero Tom Ryan is an arrogant, sadistic creep.  And being as the novel is written within this man's first person sarcastic stream of consciousness, I constantly and consistently wanted to punch his literal lights out.  What a psych-job!  But what kept me reading was Enright's masterful ability to use this character to tell exactly the right tale at exactly the right time and weave a complete and compelling story.

I grew up with three close brothers and the side-choosing, loyalty-challenging, imaginary world-building antics of the Ryan clan resembled my own adolescence better than I could describe it myself.  Dozens and dozens of times I simply smiled to myself and nodded, "Exactly right, Larry. That was my life."  Yet, an undercurrent simmered beneath the surface plot, established early, creeping-crawling through every event, and whispering softly 'something's not quite right here.'

When the answers do come, oh, they couldn't be more perfect.

And Mr. Enright, in case you ever happen to read this review, I want you to know how overwhelming impressed I am with the depth and breadth of your life memories, and how expertly you have woven them into the fabric of your narrative. My friends tell me I'm a decent storyteller, but you, sir, are in a whole different league.  Kudos.

I've seen this novel classified primarily as a mystery, but the core theme of Four Years from Home, by Larry Enright touches more upon the mystery of self-exploration and relationships than perhaps the typical murder mystery. The book opens with a family hearing news from Kenyon College, that the youngest son, Harry, is dead. However, there is no body to recover and Tom, the oldest son, is commissioned by the family to travel to the college and get to the bottom of what happened.

Right from the start, Tom proves to us to be a rather unlikable character, which is part of the charm of the story because with unlikable protagonists, an author then draws us in to look for how this protagonist might either be redeemed, or become likeable in spite of his unpleasant nature.

The biggest strength of this novel is that you do indeed want to find out what happened to Harry and what his life was all about during his college life. The relationship between Tom and Harry is a fascinating one, and viewing Harry through Tom's eyes from the past to present is, of course, where we learn more about Tom. The story definitely has its humorous moments. Tom holds a constant commentary in his head about all that he experiences and even if we find out about how much of a bully and a pain in the ass he is and always has been through these experiences, we also can't help but relate to many of them. Sometimes I felt it was a little bit overdone, as though he were trying to include every funny moment we remember about mischievous childhoods. However, the running commentary gave me an excellent insight into what was to come  -- which means foreshadowing well done. A great climactic twist with an odd tonal shift in the denouement.

A bit of mystery, a bit of humor, a bit of mental intrigue - by the halfway mark I was running through all kinds of theories and predictions in my head, which kept me reading - and you'll want to know how it ends, too.
summary: A bit of mystery, a bit of humor, a bit of mental intrigue.

reviewText: In the beginning it was fun to read but the main character was so unlikeable after 30% i could not stand it anymore.  The banter was fun in the beginning but then i found myself skipping more than i was reading.

I had expected a more light-hearted book from the description. To be honest I  thought I would get more laughs but that is not to say I didn't enjoy the book, in fact I was pleasantly surprised to find it was a mystery (and a mystery that kept me guessing until the end).

The antagonist nature of the main character Tom, although at times humorous, could be difficult to read. I also found it hard to read through the imaginary 'war games'(more from my own lack of interest, not necessarily a flaw of the book). The narration felt like it just switched over from an 'everyday' perspective without any warning making it hard to follow at times but I could appreciate that this was an intentional effect to represent the mind of Tom.

All in all though I did enjoy the book (especially the price).
summary: Not what I was expecting but good anyway

reviewText:
I enjoyed this book, even though at times the main character was a real jerk. I didn't like him and a couple of times during the book I was ready to stop reading. But I'm glad I didn't. Once I got pass the halfway point the book took a turn and I couldn't stop reading until I was done.

There are a lot of flashbacks that kind of just merge with the main story and it can be confusing but it will make sense in the end.

This is a great read and it's only a dollar.

This could have been a good story.  It has so much potential.  This will be only the third book in my entire life
that I cannot finish, I am about half way through and I can not take the main character anymore!
OK, I get it.  He is a smart a-s.  He is a bully. Does he have any redeeming qualities? I just cannot go any further and find out.
I will forward to the end, read the last few pages and call it quits.  You should not bother.  It is not worth your time or the price
of purchase.

This book was sad. Dealing with death is hard enough. Be healthy of mind and spirit to read this. Ex bullied might want to stay away to. Best to about this work is the way he makes being first born look as a child such as being king of the house and ruling the parents by crying etc.

Very well written and prosed beautifully.
The book slowly moves forward because there are sooo many flashbacks-all reiterating what a punk the narrator was as a child...The ending was good but the book didn't keep my attention

I was surprised by this novel and liked it very much. It all comes together at the end in a very 'Sixth Sense' kind of way. What I was attributing at the beginning to not enough editing is actually a rather brilliant description of mental illness.  Looking forward to reading more of Larry enright's work. Another work this reminds me of is Patricia Highsmith's The Amazing Mr. Ripley.

I had trouble finishing this book. I had no empathy for the main character -- too self-centered, little depth. The "mystery" toward the end was the only reason I finished it. The book took a clever turn. I don't have to like all protaganists -- but I sure would like to understand them.  Very weak effort.

I bought this book because it was only $0.99 and it sat in my Kindle for a few weeks.  Finally, yesterday I started reading it and I couldn't put it down.  It was so well written and kept me wanting to find out more until the very end when it all came together.  I didn't expect the ending it had, but it all made so much sense.  Just a very wonderful book, easy to read and couldn't put it down once I started reading.  These are the kinds of books I really like.
summary: kept me interested beginning to very end

reviewText: It was very hard to stay with the story line, every other page seemed to be talking about something different. It would be a good read for someone that likes alot of detail

This book was not what I expected at all. There were a few times I had to stop and ask myself what certain parts had to do with anything but everything eventually fell into place. I have to admit that I was not in love with the main character during the middle of the book, which is kind of a let down for me but my feelings changed as the book continued. The ending was amazing and I'm looking forward to reading more of his work.

I believe this is the only book by Larry Enright that I have read. I liked the idea of the book. The potential for greatness was there, but with the overuse of flashbacks and rambling, I would bore at times and need to skim. I got a feeling for the ending not long after Tom returned to Kenyon and loved the way the plot was twisting, but then I was totally let down by the final ending. I keep checking to make sure I wasn't accidentally skipping anything. I had to finish the book, but it was a struggle along the way.
summary: The good, the bad and the ok

reviewText: I don't want to spoil anything but this should not be in humor. It is mystery or just regular fiction. It's a good read but I was looking for a funny read on vacation so I bought a book listed in humor. I figured it was a funny, coming of age family dynamic story with a mystery twist. However that was definitely not the case. I did finish the book because I was curious and I don't regret that - some of the last 1/4 of the book takes a huge leap of faith tho.  Slightly obsessive with Kenyon though, a fictual college would have allowed more suspension of belief.
summary: Good read but why is this in humor??? Not humor at all!

reviewText:
Four Years from Home was not what I expected at all. When I first read the summary, it felt very Frank McCourt-ish, and in some ways it was. The character, Tom, takes us back to the days of his childhood when he was the king of his own little world. There are a lot of well-described memories that really puts you right in the middle of this family.

Tom's brother Harry is the PERFECT kid...until it's time for him to leave for school. Then, something strange happens and from there, things get complicated. I don't want to give away the story, but I will say that the book quickly turns from a very charming memoir-style story to a bit of a thriller. You have questions and you're dying to have them answered because something's just not adding up.

I was very surprised at the ending, and I would recommend this book to anyone.
summary: A Very Charming Story with a Shock!

reviewText:
I really enjoyed this book.  I agree with some of the other reviewers that an editor can make this a great book, but in all, I thought it well written.
The character, writing his "Book of Tom", has an acerbic wit and is right out of the Little Rascals. Some of his childhood antics are funny.  He can be obnoxious at times but that is all part of why the story works.
I found his childhood memories and the sharp wit used to describe them very realistic.
I must admit I was a bit confused the last few chapters (then again, I was finishing it on a plane and very tired) but the ending was quite touching.
It was part mystery and part fiction memoir. Again, a sharp witted writer who will hopefully put more out for us to try.

I bought this because the reviews were so good. I don't understand this!
The lead character is not likeable at all.
There are so many holes in the story that I don't see how it got past a book editor. The main character says he would have been voted Most Likely To Go Postal - a term not developed until the 90's. He also talked about a Happy Meal at McDonalds of Chicken Nuggets. These were not even marketed until 1979 (Happy Meal) and 1983 (Chicken Nuggets. And he parked in a handicap parking place? I never saw those either until the late 80's. Those little things I find annoying. I would never recommend this book.

While the narrator's voice is compelling and his description of time and place, spot on, "Four Years From Home" is an excellent short story that's been padded into a mediocre book.

The "surprise" twist ending becomes clear about halfway through, and the rest is just the same sequence of events reiterated over and over again with slight variations until you arrive at the inevitable conclusion.
summary: A great short story stretched and padded into a mediocre book

reviewText: I pretty much came across this book by accident and thought that I'd read it because it wasn't too expensive and thought I'd give it a shot.  It turned out to be a pretty good book.  Not the best book I've ever read but it definitely held my attention and had a few twists and turns that were out of the ordinary.  I'd recommend it to others!

Four Years From Home, by Larry Enright, is a fascinating novel. A departure from the usual formulaic, cookie-cutter mystery, this story differs greatly from anything I've ever read before. FYFH would be difficult, if not impossible, to define, in terms of assigning it a specific genre. Interestingly enough, that's exactly what I liked about it.

Much like life itself, the story unfolds in a very unpredictable way. Depending on a particular reader's perspective, one may find the main character to be humerous, or feel absolutely repulsed by him and his actions. I expect most will have mixed feelings about Tom Ryan. However, his character traits and actions provide the astute reader with a myriad of clues as to where the story may end.
The genius of Mr. Enright's novel---perhaps one in ten-thousand will ever intuit it's conclusion before arrival at the end reveal...bravo.

This was a book very hard to classify, but I guess a suspense thriller would be as close as I could get.  This book is a look into a family's nooks and crannies, through the eyes of the eldest son.  The youngest son is missing, assumed to be dead, and many twists and turns lead to a surprising conclusion.  It was hard for me to put the book down the last few chapters.
Loved the characters and all their strange quirks.  The story evolved much differently than predicted and I give it two big thumbs up for surprising me.

Every few years I read a book that just grips me and this is my new "book of the year."  I laughed aloud, cried copious tears, and in-between could not put it down.

It is the story of two brothers, the older a self-centered bully, the younger a near perfect kid everyone loves.  The story alternates between the present day  (early seventies) and flashbacks to their childhood. While I agree with some reviewers that at times the flashbacks ramble a bit too much, and I did skim a few of them, on the whole they are very important for setting the personalities, characters, and relationship of the two brothers.

At times I was confused as to what was happening, but this is not uncommon in a mystery style book; in this case my confusion mirrored that of the main character because he, too, was having difficulty assimilating all the events.

I would have liked a little more wrap-up at the end, but in reality I think this is really because I had so much crawled into the characters' skins that I was reluctant to leave.

This book isn't perfect: it could use some tighter editing.  But the story is so captivating and original, the characters so alive, becoming part of my life, and still living within me almost three months later, that the rest become minor details.  I loved it.
I love it when an author takes me on a journey filled with surprises. Mr. Enright, you have done exactly that. Thanks!

It's not very well written.  It's like the author had a good idea, but didn't know how to execute the idea.  The plot is interesting, and cold have been a very good story in someone else's hands.  The characters are not developed enough for you to be invested in them, and some are abandon in plot towards the end.  It would have been better edited down to a short story.

This book for me was a great story. I loved the family and the place Tom had made for himself. My problem with the book is the clutter. The story could have been told without the back and forth which kept me confused as to what decade I was in. I understand the author's need to include Tom's one track mind of "Combat". It just seems that a lot of that could have been left out and more of the story could have revolved and Tom and Harry outside the family.
The book was fast paced and definitely kept my interest. I would have liked to have read more of the story that was in he summation at the end.

I was looking at Amazon.com Kindle books and came upon Four Years From Home.....I read some of the reviews...saw the price was only 99 cents, and went for it...I had no expectations and figured I'd give it a try.

To my surprise, I couldn't put the book down.  Each page left you wondering what was really going on, and so I'd rush to get to the next page. I did not expect the ending at all.  This should be made into a movie.

Please do yourself a favor and buy this book.  I don't think you'll be disappointed.  Would love to read other books by this author, but read that this is his first published book....Keep em coming Mr. Enright....this was a winner!

I really enjoyed this story.  It has an unusual plot line with a find-the-missing-person theme.  Seems like it's going ahead in a pretty straightforward way, then ZIG! ZAG! Major unexpected twists and turns.

I read fiction partly to see the world through another's eyes, to get inside another's head and experience other's thoughts, emotions, and reactions in a personal way.  It's a challenge for any author to make that happen, especially with an unlovable character, but Larry Enright has done it.  The narrator, Tom,  is a nasty, narcissistic troublemaker.  Though I didn't like him any better as the book went on, I did understand him better (his sense of humor is dark and snarky, but funny, which helps). The best part is when he starts to understand his brother's life better.  Many humorous scenes and fantasies as he wrestles with the questions, "Who was my brother?" and "What do I have to do to find out more?" Tom skips way over the line into Inappropriate Land many times, but it's very entertaining. (Another reason to love fiction: the imaginative experience of  doing outrageous things.  And getting away with it!)

Readers who like to think about morals and consequences and paths chosen will enjoy this book. Readers who like to see inside the narrator's head and observe the vortex of beliefs, choices, and relationships with others will enjoy it, too. Those who like quick-paced stories with lots of surprises but vey little violence, sex, or cursing will also like it.

The ending was too tangled for me.  A clever one (didn't see that coming!) but felt more like a plot device than an ending that flows naturally from the story.  Other than that, I'd give it 4 stars for sure.

This book was not at all how I thought it was going to be. There is a lot of rambling and you would think that the writer/story-teller had ADD or something. About 3/4 of the way through I began to get really confused and it wasn't until the last 5-10 pages that everything gets cleared up. However, it leaves me with this undecided feeling about the book. I do think it was a well written book, but I didn't like the rambling.

I'm over half through the book and am debating not finishing.  If it were a real book I would just turn to the last chapter but since it's an ebook I haven't done that....yet!  In the beginning I enjoyed the banter but it's gotten old, really old.  Enough already, get to the actual story.  In 25 years of being an avid reader I've only stopped before the end of a book maybe 2 or 3 times...

It is really hard to tell.  I wanted to read it for the story, but really the book just rambles on and on in the narrator's head about the same stuff over and over and in the end it is not quite clear whether that is significant or not.  I mean, it doesn't even seem necessary.  It also seems like the author could not choose an ending and so there are sort of two endings... I guess you pick the explanation you like best?

I would say read a chapter or two in the beginning and then continue somewhere between chapter 10 and 12.  The rest doesn't seem very significant at all or absolutely necessary anyway and I don't even like skimming books.  I only skimmed when 50 or 60% through it the narrator was still rambling and then I would just skip over the flashbacks.  I gave it 3 stars only because the intrigue is enough to make me finish the story.  Unfortunately, the ending is predictable, although some of the details are not and they are fun to read.  I don't think I would even recommend people spend a dollar on this book.  I wanted to like it soooo bad Larry... Sorry!
summary: I don't think I liked this book... 2.5 stars

reviewText: 'Four Years From Home' follows Tom Ryan, self-proclaimed king of his own little world, as he investigates the mysterious circumstances surrounding the death of his younger brother Harry. It is one of the most unique stories I've read in a long, long time. Enright has created a novel that is in equal parts comedy, drama and msystery. Such a genre bender can tricky to pull off, but in this case the gamble pays off. 'Four Years From Home' is laugh-out-loud funny, deeply moving and ultimately shocking. If this sounds vague, it's because revealing more would make it neccessary to give away a very sigificant plot point that links these elements together and that readers ought to discover for themselves. It's definitely worth it!

I was really into the book at the beginning, but toward the middle it started getting really lackluster.  I am sure that someone who is really into the military might beg to differ, but I found myself skimming through descriptions.  I see where the author was going with this tactic, but I just wasn't picking up what he was throwing down.  For being 99 it wasn't too bad.  It just wasn't holding my interest, but I plowed through and finished it.

This engrossing tale is told entirely in first-person narrative, from the perspective of Tom Ryan. It is the story of Tom, told by Tom, starring Tom ... you get the idea. It's his world and he's the only important person in it; the other inhabitants of the world -the bit players - only matter if they are of use to Tom. Though not entirely original, Tom's tale is well-paced and suspenseful, with the exception of the last few chapters, which dragged a bit, with unnecessary details and flashbacks that didn't contribute to the story. There were times when I almost gave up and quit reading - I admit that I go overboard pouncing on mistakes I find, from typos to inconsistencies and implausibilities in the story, stubbornly refusing to finish a book over obvious or egregious errors. I caught on to some apparent discrepancies, but plot exposition neatly accounted for most of them. It was tempting to skip to the end as the pace got sluggish (the flashbacks were getting tedious and I just wanted my questions answered), but I didn't, and it was worth the effort to keep reading. The problem with writing a review for this particular story is that I don't want to give away any of the plot twists or revelations. The plot twists are inventive and although I had a general idea of how the mystery was going to turn out, the end still held some surprises. There is some foreshadowing of the final reveal, but the author holds enough back so that even the most astute reader can't guess exactly what's coming, but not enough that a novice reader will feel misled or cheated. Overall, I would recommend this book for its premise, readability and believability, even if it falls short of being perfect.
summary: The story of Tom Ryan, by Tom Ryan, starring Tom Ryan....

reviewText: I find so many hidden treasures in the free ebooks. This one is certainly a rare jewel: mult-facited, spell-binding, and in the end, truly beautiful. Beyond that, I dare not share one strand, or the story will unravel.

It began well enough - but then the main character just kept rambling on and on.  The more he went on, the less it kept my interest.  Like another reviewer, I skimmed over a great deal of it, which is something I NEVER usually do.  The ending brought the plot together, but almost was not worth what took to get there.
summary: Struggled to Get to the End

reviewText: The product description is 100% accurate.  What isn't mentioned is the stunning conclusion.  Tommy is unlikeable because the writer has done such a good job defining who Tommy thinks he is.  The journey he takes us on to solve the mystery of Harry shows us there is always more below the surface than we can realize. Even Tommy finds that truth.  I will be looking for more from this author.

Although I had bought this book expecting something would come out of it, I was disappointed in the meandering prose.  I was tired to death of the main character and unfortunately could not care less what happened to him.

The story seemed intriguing but it didn't take many chapters before I stopped caring.  The book is full of repeated ramblings on that are irrelevant and uninteresting.  I skimmed through 10 chapters and hadn't missed anything vital when I FINALLY arrived at the last.  Save yourself the pain and read the first and last chapter only!

I am addicted to reading and have read many books. I have never skipped pages before until this book. I couldn't wait to get to the ending which was worth it but too much rambling to get there. I did not particularly like the main character, Tom.

This was a convoluted, improbable, and bizarre story that didn't leave me at all satisfied.  The main character was intriguing but not likeable.  I don't recommend it unless your taste in books runs to the...well, convoluted, improbable, and bizarre.

I am a fan of murder mysteries and can pick loopholes and can guess killers. This is NOT a murder mystery, not a suspense novel, not....well, what it is, more importantly, is a coming of age, finding yourself tale woven into a psychological thriller. And it does not even feel like a thriller till the nagging voice in your head, which had been sensing that something is not what it seems, suddenly gets very loud.

So, Tom Ryan is a self-confessed, happy-about-it bully and I instinctively disliked him. But his matter-of-fact, quirky, and unintentionally humorous first person accounts drew me in. That's where I think the writing wins me over. The characterization, all supposedly described and hence colored by Tom's perception about them, are delightful and deep. I wish I had more knowledge of 'Combat' to enjoy this more.

As Harry and Tom's world merge and separate, along with their personalities, and lies become truths and vice versa, I almost skipped pages to get to the end.
And the end, to a seasoned mystery-reader like me, was a revelation. It was something that was hovering in my sub-conscious but still packed a punch.

Loved this book, recommended for people who can laugh at ordinary things presented with humor, loves to explore characters even when there is a suspense in the background, and mainly enjoy a good read.

The rambling nature of the story leaves the reader unfulfilled and desperate to get to the end. There was no strong connection to the characters or the story.  Not really sure I understand what others liked about it.
summary: Easy read, but a waste of time

reviewText: I bought this only because it was cheap, but it turned out to be a case of getting much more than I paid for.  Often mysteries will have no clues as to what is actually going on which I think is poor storytelling--The Usual Suspects is an exception--, but this one gave me several clues throughout.  Most of Tom's narrative is amusing, but the dramatic parts are dramatic; I was grinning or crying through most of the book.  Yes, I would recommend this to friends.

This is probably the hardest book review I'll ever write.  As an author myself I always preface my reviews with the information of whether I know the author or not.  I've "met" Larry Enright on Facebook, Twitter and a variety of other forums.  I love his wit and sense of humor.  I've interviewed him and didn't take offense to his comment that my writing career was inspired by a Rabid Dog ("Old Yeller").  And I'm not a professional reviewer.

When I told Larry that I had purchased his book he emailed me and told me it was "Different", and he hoped I liked it.

Different would be one way of describing "Four Years From Home".  Most people assume since I write dark, not-so-cozy murder mysteries that my taste in literature runs the gamut of James Patterson, Tami Hoag, Kay Hooper, Patricia Cornwell and other mystery writers with a penchant for murder and mayhem.  They would be right to a certain extent, but I also loved C. S. Lewis.  The first time I read "The Screw Tape Letters" I was amazed, thrilled and awed by a work of literary art so deep, and so exquisite  I almost felt I should chop off my fingers for even considering myself to be an author.  "The Screw Tape Letters" was different.  A book that inspired great passion in those who read it, and those who attempted to read it and burned it as blasphemy.  Growing up in the Bible belt I naturally assumed it would burst into flames as soon as I opened it, or at the very least I would be stricken with some horrible malady for reading such "trash".  It has a place of honor on my bookshelf as being one of the true literary arts of my time, and the exact opposite of what I was led to believe.  That's all I can say about it without giving you spoilers.

Several years ago a movie came out called "Sixth Sense".  Millions of people watched this movie before I did, but out of millions of reviews not one person gave away the spoiler.  That fascinated me.  It was definitely "different".  And millions of people kept that secret religiously.  There were minor clues along the way, but so intricately weaved into the story that you missed them.

Which brings me back to "Four Years From Home".  A work of literary art which I believe will inspire passion within each reader.  You will love it - or you will hate it.  Or perhaps like me you will love it and hate it (which I can't say why without giving away a spoiler).  Within the pages of "Four Years From Home" Mr. Enright has weaved an intricate model of human hopes, dreams, fears, strengths and weaknesses.  The brilliance of the human mind, and the frailty of the human mind.

Tom Ryan is a Legend In His Own Mind.  Much like every child and artistic adult who grew up in an atmosphere that allows the imagination to develop and grow.  Reality is just a figment of our imagination to be bent, changed and shaped to our will.  But somewhere deep inside, perhaps at the core of our existence, deep within the soul lies a reality we cannot bend; we cannot change or shape to our will.  A reality we can only at best attempt to run away from and escape.

I can't say more without giving away a spoiler, which is why this was a very difficult review to write.

OVERALL BOOK - 4.5 Stars

I gave this 4.5 stars instead of 5 because I found at least 5 typos in the book were words were omitted from a sentence and in one case transposed in a sentence.  For a debut novel this is minor, as my own traditionally published first book had 7 typos.  When I brought this to the attention of my publisher the comeback was, "Patricia Cornwell's new book has 28 typos in it."  My comeback was, "I'm not Patricia Cornwell."  As authors we have a responsibility to our readers.  As self-published authors that responsibility, in my humble opinion, increases.

CHARACTERIZATION - 5 Stars

You are immediately drawn into the Ryan family through Tom's internal dialogue, and through interaction with his mother, father, sisters and brothers.  You're given a clear-- at least according to the legend-- concise "picture" of the family and their strengths and weaknesses.  They each become someone you feel you know intimately.  Especially Harry.  Sweet, special Harry.

  Although some may consider this a backdoor approach into characterization, it worked for me.

PLOT - 5 Stars

The plot is "different".  If you're a traditional mystery follower who expects certain things to happen in order, you may be slightly disappointed.  But the plot is unique.  A true literary art, as it is subtle, and perhaps somewhat hidden in the Legend's mind.  And the purpose of a mystery is to lead the reader down a path of intrigue, throwing out subtle clues and yet revealing nothing that will allow you to grasp the conclusion--therein, Mr. Enright has excelled.  I, as a mystery writer, applaud myself on being able to figure out early on "what's going on".  That didn't happen here.  I was tempted many times to move to the end of the book, but as with all books I enjoy I denied myself that pleasure and kept turning pages.  Searching for the clues that would reveal the end.  I was astounded.  I would never have guessed the ending.

This was a difficult book to review because I loved it, and I hated it, and I wanted to tell you why, but much like "Sixth Sense", that would reveal far too much.  You may find yourself a little irritated by Tom's obsession with (oops, can't say, because that's a spoiler), but if you like "different" then I truly believe you'll love this book.  A fantastic debut novel, and one I'm glad I didn't miss.
summary: You'll Love It - Or You'll Hate it

reviewText: I'll start with the good.  I finished this book because I really was interested in the outcome.  The ending was not what I expected, which is a good thing.  The problem is, I found myself skimming through the middle ramblings to get to the real story.  Truthfully, although I was interested in the main story, getting through it was sometimes painful.  Glad I'm done.
Dont waste your time on this one. I'm half way through and cant take it anymore. This book is all ramblings with hardly any story so to speak.

I truly love a good read. Unfortunately, the story line was painfully thin here. The characters were wooden. I did a lot of skimming (not something I usually do) to get to the meat of the story. There was so much puffery in the form of the main character's boyhood reflections, and they became repetitive and tiresome.
If I hadn't seen who the author was, I would have suspected that it was written by a college freshman---it was that bad! Amazed that there were so many recommendations. Were they written by friends and relatives of the author? Very puzzled.

The book rambled quite a bit, which I found frustrating, but the twists and turns are great. I figured the ending out about half way through the book, but the reasons behind the deception were the real surprizes. A good read.
This isn't my type of book. An adult narrating in the style of an eight year old boy. It does work though and I was pleasatly surprised how much I enjoyed it.
I haver read a little over one third of this book and I am ready to quit. It is just plain bad. MY question is how the auther got 20 people to give it five stars.

If it hadn't been for the enthusiastic reviews, I wouldn't have made it over the setup "hump" in Four Years from Home. With some encouragement from other reviewers, I stayed with it and found the middle and ending interesting. One reviewer mentions an Epilogue, which appears to show up as Chapter 14 in my Kindle for PC, version 6 display. The ending I have is precipitous and less than satisfying. A good first effort, and quite original in concept. Has its funny moments. After the slow start, it moves well and is rather gripping.

This is the first review I have written for a book, but I loved this book so much I thought I should tell everyone. I couldn't put it down once I started. Grabs you right from the beginning. I was totally blown away when the mysterey was finally revealed. I highly recommend!
ONE OF THE BEST BOOKS I HAVE EVER READ.  IT HAD EVERYTHING - LOVE, PASSION, FANTASY, HISTORICAL FACTS.  I WOULD RECOMMEND IT TO ANYONE.  CANNOT WAIT FOR MR. ENRIGHT'S NEXT BOOK!!

Even though I am a female I instantly identified with Tom. I was born in the same year, 1946, and am the oldest of five children. I was often a bully to my siblings (although not as physical as he was) and thought of myself as entitled and resented the existance of "the others". Tom's parents also reminded me of my own....I guess because of the era we grew up in. Also the small college Harry attended was much like the one I graduated from in 1968.
The story was so interesting, and Tom's imagination was so outrageous that I read the book really quickly. I love the twists and turns in the plot, quite a story. Very well written, a great book.

You could call this book a humorous look at the familial bonds between a self-described bully and his siblings. You could call it a wrenching tale of loss and discovery. You could call it a story of twists and turns that both entrances and shocks.

You'd be right on all counts.

The author seems purposed to not only share the story of bully/brother Tom Ryan, but to put us in Tom's head as his world is turned upside down, and as his grasp of it is peeled away bit by bit. We don't just follow Tom's journey--we inhabit it as he seeks out answers to his brother Harry's death while away at college. What we get from this masterfully told tale is always touching, frequently worthy of chuckles born of our own memories of childhood, and also impossible to anticipate. I did not see coming what transpired.

Highly, highly recommended. You will be hooked from the first paragraph of this tale that should be treasured.

A mystery unfolds over the holidays at the Ryan house when all but one of the Ryan kids return to celebrate.  The youngest, Harry, the golden child, has been out of the house attending college out of state- never to return, as the family is informed by college officials that Harry has died in an unfortunate accident.

Oldest child, Tom, is sent to find out what really happened.  Story enough in itself, except that Tom Ryan is one of the most self centered, egotistical bullies you could imagine. As the oldest child, Tom ruled his world with an iron fist and all those around him are but minions to complete his latest reign of terror, his own siblings obstacles to his supreme position in the family.  In his delusional world, Tom is the king and everyone and everything is designed around him, about him and for him.  The first clue into the depth of Tom's ego is his ongoing conversation with himself.  Constantly arranging and rearranging his rules to suit the moment, loses are acceptable as long as the end result is a gain for Tom.  When Tom's world enters Harry's world, the collision of the mind in epic and unfolds into an act that only Harry could understand, and he's not there to explain it.
So is Harry dead?  Is Tom going to uncover what happened in the four years Harry has been gone?
That will be up to you to determine if you read Four Years From Home, by Larry Enright.
summary: Four Years From Home is More Than Enough

reviewText:
I love a challenge.  So when the other reviewers said the ending was such a shock, I was determined to figure it out ahead of time.  And -- aha!! -- no, not so much.  I came close, but Larry Enright (author) had some stuff up his sleeve I didn't quite see coming.  Thank goodness.  It was so much better that way.

***Small spoiler alert*** The last chapter was brilliant.  How do you write madness when you're writing in first person?  I was reading so fast I would suddenly realize I was holding my breath.  And the epilogue - all dialogue - was masterfully done.  A great wrap-up of the details.

A story of family, honor, redemption, sanity, and insanity.  I found myself annoyed part way through at the first person accounts of the narrator's bad boy deeds, but the stories, and his voice in the telling of them, all work together in the end.

As one reviewer said, not a perfect book.  But I can't remember the last time I read an entire book in one day -- and not because it was so short, but because I couldn't make myself stop.

Thank you, Larry, for characters I will keep in my head for a long while....

Who exactly is Tom Ryan?  A bratty trouble-maker a or a borderline schizophrenic? The black sheep of the family or a caring brother?  As you read this book you realize that nothing really is what it appears to be on the surface.

Larry Enright has written a book that is both laugh-out-loud funny and poignant,  A brilliant first novel that really makes you think about life and relationships.  This is one book that I'm going to recommend to my friends.

Larry Enright's masterpiece 'Four Years from home' takes the reader on a wild ride of gut-wrenching emotions. Humorous in parts, dramatic and thought-provoking, its central driving force is a dark mystery that unfolds at about chapter 6 and continues onward to its stunning conclusion.
